clinicalPearls: Most cases are epithelial in origin, and high-grade serous carcinoma, now thought largely to arise from the distal fallopian tube, is the commonest and most aggressive subtype

Symptoms are frequently vague and persistent, including abdominal bloating, early satiety, pelvic or abdominal discomfort, and urinary urgency, so a high index of suspicion is needed particularly in women over fifty
Because there is no reliable early symptom or screening test, the majority present with advanced intra-abdominal disease
Inherited mutations in BRCA1 and BRCA2 and Lynch syndrome markedly increase lifetime risk and should prompt genetic assessment
A pelvic mass combined with ascites and a raised CA-125 in a postmenopausal woman is highly suggestive and warrants specialist referral
Management centres on maximal cytoreductive surgery to remove all visible tumour combined with platinum-based chemotherapy
Risk assessment tools that combine ultrasound features, menopausal status, and CA-125 help triage women to gynaecological oncology
Germ cell and sex cord-stromal tumours are important in younger women and can produce hormonal effects or tumour markers such as AFP, hCG, or inhibin
reference.pathophysiology: High-grade serous ovarian cancer is now believed to originate frequently from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma in the fimbrial end of the fallopian tube, with early TP53 mutation and genomic instability, often in the context of homologous recombination deficiency from BRCA pathway defects. Malignant cells exfoliate and disseminate across the peritoneal cavity, seeding the omentum, bowel serosa, and diaphragm, producing ascites through increased vascular permeability and lymphatic obstruction. Other histological types arise from ovarian surface epithelium, germ cells, or sex cord-stromal cells with distinct biology.
additionalDifferentials: Uterine fibroids or other pelvic mass
Metastatic gastrointestinal cancer to the ovary (Krukenberg tumour)
Primary peritoneal or fallopian tube carcinoma
additionalInvestigations: Transvaginal and transabdominal pelvic ultrasound to characterise the mass
Serum CA-125 and, in younger women, germ cell markers (AFP, hCG, LDH) and inhibin
CT of the abdomen and pelvis to assess disease extent and operability
Risk-of-malignancy scoring combining ultrasound, menopausal status and tumour markers
Histological confirmation from surgical specimen or image-guided biopsy where surgery is not upfront
Genetic testing for BRCA and mismatch repair mutations
redFlags: Rapidly accumulating ascites with breathlessness or abdominal distension
Bowel obstruction from peritoneal or omental disease
Marked weight loss and cachexia suggesting advanced malignancy
Pleural effusion indicating spread beyond the abdomen
A complex solid-cystic pelvic mass with markedly elevated CA-125 in a postmenopausal woman
reference.prognosis: Overall survival is dominated by stage at presentation and by the completeness of surgical cytoreduction; disease confined to the ovary is potentially curable, whereas widespread peritoneal disease carries a poorer outlook despite platinum sensitivity. Tumour grade, histological subtype, and BRCA/homologous recombination status influence response to chemotherapy and to maintenance agents such as PARP inhibitors, and relapse is common in advanced disease.
pitfalls: Dismissing persistent bloating and abdominal symptoms in older women as functional bowel disturbance
Assuming a normal CA-125 excludes malignancy, as it can be normal in early or non-serous tumours
Rupturing or morcellating an undiagnosed malignant cyst during surgery
Failing to refer suspicious masses to a gynaecological oncology centre before intervention
Overlooking germ cell tumours in young women by not checking age-appropriate tumour markers
management: Maximal cytoreductive surgery aiming to remove all visible tumour, performed either upfront or as interval debulking after neoadjuvant chemotherapy
Platinum-based chemotherapy, typically carboplatin with paclitaxel, as the backbone of systemic treatment
PARP-inhibitor maintenance for BRCA-mutated or homologous-recombination-deficient disease, with anti-angiogenic bevacizumab in selected cases
Serial CA-125 alongside cross-sectional imaging to monitor treatment response and detect relapse
Genetic testing for BRCA and mismatch-repair mutations, with cascade family testing and risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy for carriers
Manage symptomatic ascites with paracentesis and provide early palliative and supportive care in advanced disease
Coordinate care through a gynaecological-oncology multidisciplinary team
